doc.title: Dick Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006

title: Favorite Dixieland players and Chicago versus New Orleans style
summary: He names Condon-style heroes, explains two-beat New Orleans versus four-to-the-bar Chicago style, and tells young drummers to leave two-beat bands.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Neat. Do you have favorite Dixieland musicians yourself?

Yes. I would say Wild Bill Davison, Bobby Hackett on cornet and on trombone I would say Cutty Cutshall and Lou McGarrity, on clarinet it would be Edmond Hall and let me think, you’ve got the idea. This is the Eddie Condon type player.
Right, right. Do you make a distinction between New Orleans Dixieland and what came after when it went to Chicago? Does it sound different to you?

Sure. Much different. More refined and it’s more of a four-to-the-bar beat. There were a lot of two-beat guys that came from New Orleans with the Preservation Hall type thing. The old style, traditional. Then it went to Chicago and by the time I heard it it was in Manhattan and it was sizzling my ears off, I couldn’t go back in time any more than that. I loved it.
Well if a young drummer came to you and said, “They’re telling me to play two-beat here. I don’t know what to do.” What do you tell them.
Wow. If he’s telling me that I’d say forget it.
Really. Find a different bunch of guys?
